name: QPrompt
product: QPrompt by Cuperino

evidence.says: The official 2.0.4 download section provides separate macOS disk images for Apple Silicon and Intel.
The developer's November 16, 2026 release announcement identifies 2.0.4 as the preferred stable version and links its Apple Silicon build.

name: Kindle Comic Converter
product: Kindle Comic Converter (KCC), maintained by Alex Xu and the KCC project

evidence.says: The official 13.0.4 release assets include kcc_macos_arm_13.0.4.dmg and a separate Intel Mac image.
The project identifies kcc_macos_arm disk images as the builds for Apple Silicon Macs.

name: HakuNeko Desktop
product: HakuNeko Desktop by the manga-download project

evidence.says: The project labels its latest stable HakuNeko client unmaintained and points users to the separate HaruNeko beta.
Release 6.1.7 was published on 2020-01-18 and its only macOS asset is the Intel amd64 disk image.

limitation: Rosetta operation was not verified.
notes: HaruNeko is the project's successor beta and has its own releases.

name: datovka
product: Datovka by CZ.NIC

evidence.says: CZ.NIC announced Datovka 4.30.2 on 2026-11-15.
CZ.NIC's versioned download directory includes datovka-4.30.2-arm64-macos13.3.dmg.

notes: The ARM disk image targets macOS 13.3 and later.

name: RECentral
product: RECentral for Mac by AVerMedia

evidence.says: AVerMedia lists RECentral for Mac 1.2.21 for macOS 10.9–10.13 and explicitly excludes macOS 10.14 and later.
AVerMedia has a separate product page for the later RECentral Express app.
Static inspection of the official 1.2.21 disk image matched com.AVerMedia.RECentral and found a 32-bit i386 Mach-O at RECentral.app/Contents/MacOS/RECentral.

notes: This entry matches the original capture application for the Live Gamer Portable, distinct from RECentral Express.

name: Ray
product: Ray desktop debugger by Spatie

evidence.says: Spatie dates the Ray 4.0.0 release to November 24, 2026 and lists native macOS builds for Apple Silicon and Intel.
Spatie’s macOS download link redirects to the official version 4.0.0 universal DMG.

notes: Ray 4 imports settings and archives from Ray 3 on first launch.

name: EZbass
product: EZbass standalone bass instrument by Toontrack

evidence.says: Toontrack dates the current 1.3.4 release to May 29, 2026 and distributes it through Product Manager.
Toontrack explicitly added native 64-bit ARM support to the standalone app in 1.1.0.
The current product page lists both Intel and Apple silicon for the macOS product and confirms that the standalone edition is included.

name: WSM
product: Wireless Systems Manager (WSM) by Sennheiser

evidence.says: Sennheiser lists setup 4.9.0-13 as its Mac download.
The 4.9.0 manual says that installation adds Rosetta on Apple silicon because WSM uses Intel components.

limitation: The manual establishes Rosetta as required for the app but does not enumerate the main executable's architecture slices.
notes: 4.9.0-13 is the advertised macOS installer build.

name: Save to Pocket
product: Save to Pocket Safari extension by Mozilla / Read It Later

evidence.says: MacUpdater identifies com.pocket.safari.save version 1.1 as an Intel Mac container for the Safari extension and reports its store delisting.
Pocket's publisher confirms that its shutdown included the Pocket browser extensions.

notes: This bundle exists to install a Safari extension. The Pocket service is also shut down.

name: BeardedSpice
product: BeardedSpice media-key controller by the BeardedSpice project

evidence.says: The official release supplies BeardedSpice-2.2.3.zip, whose BeardedSpice.app/Contents/MacOS/BeardedSpice has a single x86_64 Mach-O slice.
A user reports that the official app works under Rosetta 2 on an M1 Mac mini.

limitation: The runtime report is from 2021 and does not establish present-day support for individual media services.
notes: Contributor-built universal binaries and the separate Beardie app are not official BeardedSpice releases.

name: Flipper
product: Flipper Electron desktop debugger by Meta (formerly Facebook Sonar)

evidence.says: Meta marks the repository archived and identifies 0.239.0 as the last Electron desktop release.
The release's Flipper-mac.dmg contains com.facebook.sonar 0.239.0 with an x86_64-only Flipper.app/Contents/MacOS/Flipper executable.

notes: The final matching Electron app was Intel-only. The Apple Silicon Flipper-server disk images package the browser-based server variant.

name: Sideloadly!
product: Sideloadly desktop app by the Sideloadly team

evidence.says: The official Mac download SideloadlySetup.dmg contains io.sideloadly.sideloadly 0.72, and Sideloadly.app/Contents/MacOS/Sideloadly is an x86_64-only Mach-O executable.
The vendor reports running the desktop app on Apple silicon Macs and testing on Big Sur, Monterey, and Ventura.

limitation: The official page advertises 0.71.0 and provides no release date for the 0.72 binary it delivered.
notes: The architecture is for the desktop tool. Apple silicon support in the marketing copy also describes the Mac as a target for sideloaded iOS apps.

name: Truple
product: Truple screenshot accountability for macOS by Truple LLC

evidence.says: Truple says its original macOS app reached end of maintenance and directs customers to ScreenKin or Best Accountability.
Truple still offers legacy installers for older macOS versions and instructs users to disable app updates.

limitation: The final legacy build's exact version and executable architecture were not established.
notes: ScreenKin and Best Accountability are separately distributed replacements.

name: UJAM
product: UJAM App plug-in manager by UJAM Music Technology GmbH

evidence.says: UJAM's download page advertises version 1.2.12 and offers separate ARM64 and Intel Mac installers.
UJAM dates 1.2.12 to July 20, 2026, records native Apple Silicon support from 1.0.0, and lists the newer 1.2.13 update.

limitation: The public product page labels the ARM64 download 1.2.12; the changelog lists 1.2.13 without a version-specific Mac installer.
notes: The record covers the app manager. The product page also includes a general Rosetta requirement, which does not identify an architecture for individual plug-ins.

name: NOW TV
product: NOW Player for macOS by Sky UK, formerly NOW TV Player

evidence.says: Sky's current PC and Mac viewing guide directs customers to supported web browsers and lists no standalone player download.
The July 2023 report documents Sky replacing the separate NOW Player with browser playback.

limitation: The final player release and its binary architecture were not verified.
notes: The NOW streaming service continues through supported desktop browsers.

name: FAHControl
product: FAHControl advanced control panel for Folding@home v7

evidence.says: Folding@home says the current browser-based Web Control replaces the separate FAHControl app and recommends migrating from v7.
The official archive's final macOS v7 package, fah-installer_7.6.21_x86_64.mpkg.zip, contains an x86_64-only FAHControl.app/Contents/MacOS/FAHControl executable.

notes: The final macOS FAHControl app was Intel-only. Folding@home still distributes legacy v7 files in its archive.

name: Grim Fandango Remastered
product: Grim Fandango Remastered by Double Fine Productions, GOG Mac edition

evidence.says: GOG's build service lists 1.4.0 (A), published September 8, 2020, as the newest public Mac build for product 1207667183.
Double Fine gives x86-family processor requirements for the Mac release.
A GOG customer reports that the Mac release runs through Rosetta on an M1 Mac.

limitation: Customer launch reports differ, and the successful report does not specify a macOS version or independently establish compatibility on current macOS.
notes: 1.4.0 (A) is the GOG release label. The scan's 2.3.0.6 is the GOGLauncher bundle version.

name: FoundryLicenseUtility
product: Foundry Licensing Utility (FLU) by Foundry

evidence.says: Foundry lists FoundryLicensingUtility_8.1.6.dmg as its current macOS licensing utility and identifies the new build as a rebuild of the FLU.
Static inspection of build 8.1.6.241 found that FoundryLicensingUtility.app/Contents/MacOS/FoundryLicensingUtility is a thin x86_64 Mach-O.

limitation: Rosetta operation of the licensing utility was not verified.
notes: The same utility now uses bundle ID com.foundry.flu; the historical scanner entry uses uk.co.thefoundry.FoundryLicenseUtility.

name: JabberVDI
product: Cisco Jabber Softphone for VDI macOS thin client by Cisco Systems

evidence.says: Cisco's download table offers a single x64 macOS thin client for the row labeled 15.2.
Static package inspection found the exact com.cisco.JabberVDI bundle ID and build 12.9.0.310904 in Info.plist and a thin x86_64 executable at JabberVDI.app/Contents/MacOS/vxc.
Cisco documents M1 and M2 compatibility in the 14.1 VDI requirements.

limitation: Cisco's hardware support notes could not be tied to the exact inspected package build, and its Rosetta operation was not verified.
notes: Cisco's 15.2 download row serves a package with older internal bundle and installer versions. The separate Cisco Jabber desktop app has its own support status.

name: Youku Mac
product: Youku Mac (优酷 Mac desktop client) by Youku

evidence.says: Youku's official client download page labels its Mac build V9.5.6.1001 without identifying its CPU architecture.

limitation: No architecture-specific installer, official statement, or inspectable download for this exact desktop build was verified.
notes: The App Store mobile client and the aDrive and Alipay cask hints are separate products.

name: Instagram Downloader
product: Instagram Downloader attributed to Bao Nguyen by the historical listing metadata
limitation: No current official release, maintainer page, or architecture evidence was found for baonguyen.Instagram-Downloader.
notes: The scan is for version 1.0. Same-name downloaders from other authors do not establish this bundle's status.

name: Teambition
product: Teambition desktop client by Alibaba’s DingTalk / Teambition

evidence.says: The live Teambition homepage’s embedded configuration identifies a single Mac download for version 2.0.3 under darwin/x64.
Inspection of Teambition.app/Contents/MacOS/Teambition and Info.plist in the official DMG found matching bundle ID and version 2.0.3 with an x86_64-only Mach-O.

limitation: I found no vendor statement or credible runtime report confirming Rosetta 2 compatibility.
notes: The macOS installer remains accessible from the vendor configuration and Homebrew.

name: cnlabSpeedTest
product: cnlab UX Test (Speedtest) desktop app by cnlab AG

evidence.says: cnlab offers separate macOS 64-bit and macOS ARM64 downloads for its desktop UX Test.
The linked desktop release history lists 3.5.2 as the latest release, dated October 23, 2026.
The vendor’s current ARM64 DMG responds successfully and reports an October 23, 2026 modification date matching the latest desktop release.

notes: The download is more than 150 MB, so the main executable was not inspected.

name: EasyFileDateChanger
product: Easy File Date Changer by Wolfgang Schwarz (IMC Media)

evidence.says: The Mac App Store identifies Wolfgang Schwarz and lists 1.0.2 as the latest release with no architecture or Rosetta statement.

limitation: The store exposes neither architecture metadata nor an official standalone binary that could be inspected.

name: AdwareCleaner
product: Adware Cleaner – Remove Adware, Spyware, and Restore Your Browser by Pocket Bits LLC

evidence.says: Apple’s lookup maps the exact bundle ID to Pocket Bits LLC’s Mac app and identifies version 1.2 dated March 24, 2016.
The developer’s product page links to the Mac App Store and gives macOS 10.10 as its minimum requirement without naming a processor architecture.

limitation: No architecture for this product’s listed build or confirmed Rosetta 2 runtime was found.
notes: The developer advertises native updates for some products, but the Adware Cleaner page still points to version 1.2.

name: MPKMini Mk2 Editor
product: MPK Mini mkII Editor by Akai Professional (inMusic)

evidence.says: Akai’s legacy downloads list the Mac MPK Mini mkII Editor at version 1.0.5.
Akai’s Big Sur matrix supports the MPK mini mkII hardware on M1 but explicitly excludes its editor.
Akai’s Tahoe matrix explicitly lists the MPK Mini mkII Editor as unsupported on Apple Silicon.

limitation: Akai’s Monterey table labels the editor in testing, and I found no later positive capability statement or official binary architecture.
notes: The compatibility of the controller as a MIDI device and the separate mkIII Editor do not apply to this listing.

name: Wormhole
product: Wormhole phone mirroring and control by Viper Gaming Studio

evidence.says: The vendor links WormholeInstaller.dmg as its Mac download, and inspection found that Wormhole.app/Contents/MacOS/Wormhole from that disk image is an x86_64-only Mach-O executable with bundle ID er.Wormhole and version 2.1.0.
MacUpdater identifies the exact bundle and vendor, dates 2.1.0 to October 12, 2024, and labels it Intel.
The disabled Homebrew cask calls its Intel package 1.8.0 and displays a Rosetta 2 caveat.

limitation: The Homebrew compatibility statement is labeled 1.8.0, and no first-hand report confirmed launch and operation of 2.1.0 under Rosetta.
notes: The vendor's current disk image contains 2.1.0 although its public changelog and Homebrew metadata lag. This is the phone mirroring app from er.run.

name: LockDown Browser OEM
product: LockDown Browser OEM by Respondus

evidence.says: Respondus identifies OEM as the shared Mac browser distributed by its assessment partners.
Partner Hawkes identifies its installed Mac app as LockDown Browser OEM and lists its current Mac version as 2.1.6.01.
Respondus says the current Mac LockDown Browser is Intel-based and runs on Apple silicon through Rosetta.
Partner Paradigm labels its available Mac installer for the OEM edition x64c.

limitation: The Rosetta statement covers the Mac product family, and the newest OEM version verified at a partner was 2.1.6.01.
notes: OEM installation is through assessment partners. Respondus says a native Apple silicon build is in development.

name: cardPresso
product: cardPresso ID card design and printing software by cardPresso

evidence.says: The vendor lists cardPresso 1.7.140 as its latest macOS release and links to both a disk image and a ZIP.
Static inspection of cardPresso1.7.140.1.dmg inside the official ZIP found build 1.7.140.1 and a thin x86_64 Mach-O at cardPresso.app/Contents/MacOS/cardPresso.

limitation: Rosetta operation of the app and its printer drivers was not verified.
notes: The vendor page uses release version 1.7.140 and the Mac bundle identifies itself as 1.7.140.1.

name: Logitech Presentation
product: Logitech Presentation software for Spotlight and other presentation remotes by Logitech

evidence.says: Logitech says Logitech Presentation reached end of support and that supported devices migrated to Logi Options+.
Static inspection of the bundled Logitech Presentation.app/Contents/MacOS/Logitech Presentation in version 2.10.276 found a universal x86_64 and arm64 Mach-O for com.logitech.presenter.

limitation: Runtime behavior and the architecture of other auxiliary components were not verified.
notes: The final main application is native-capable. The separately bundled updater and laclient have thin Intel executables.

name: lghub
product: Logitech G HUB (lghub.app) by Logitech G

evidence.says: Logitech's Mac download entry identifies software version 2026.7.1011216.
Logitech explicitly describes the current Mac G HUB app as natively supporting Apple Silicon and Intel on macOS Sonoma and later.
The release notes date 2026.7.1011216 to October 12, 2026, and list a newer pair of cross-platform version numbers without distinguishing the Mac build.

limitation: The Mac-specific download page names 2026.7.1011216; the newer paired release-note entries do not identify which version is for Mac.
notes: The downloaded G HUB installer is a separate executable from lghub.app.

name: Jaspersoft Studio Professional
product: Jaspersoft Studio Professional (commercial edition) by Jaspersoft

evidence.says: Jaspersoft lists a commercial Mac build of Studio 9.0.2, with account-gated downloads and no architecture label.
The vendor's v9.0.0 setup guide documents a commercial x86_64 Mac installer and does not identify the architecture of the 9.0.2 download.

limitation: The architecture and Rosetta behavior of the commercial 9.0.2 Mac binary could not be verified.
notes: Community Edition packages do not establish the Professional build's architecture.

name: Wireless Workbench
product: Wireless Workbench 7 by Shure

evidence.says: Shure lists Apple Silicon compatibility for version 7.9.0 and explicitly identifies version 7.1.0 as universal and native.
Homebrew identifies the single current Mac build as 7.9.0.104, with the package filename ShureWWB_x64-mac.7.9.0.104.pkg.

limitation: Shure specifies Apple Silicon compatibility for 7.9.0 but has not stated the executable architecture for that build, and its 624 MB package exceeded the inspection limit.
notes: Shure explicitly documented a universal binary with no Rosetta requirement in 7.1.0. The current installer filename uses x64, a label that cannot establish the installed executable architecture.

name: AJ Classic
product: Animal Jam Classic desktop game by WildWorks

evidence.says: The Animal Jam Classic site distributes the Mac client separately from the newer Animal Jam game.
Inspection of AJ Classic.app/Contents/MacOS/AJ Classic and Info.plist in the official DMG found bundle ID animaljam, version 1.5.7 build 1.5.7.59, and an x86_64-only Mach-O.
Players report running AJ Classic smoothly on Apple Silicon Macs, including a MacBook Air M5 and MacBook Neo.

limitation: The community reports name their Mac models but do not give a client build number or show Rosetta process status.

name: MPlayerX
product: MPlayerX scan with bundle ID com.telephoto.identifier, publisher unverified

evidence.says: The public upstream MPlayerX release by Zongyao Qu publishes a version 1.1.1 archive.
Inspection of the upstream MPlayerX.app Info.plist and MacOS/MPlayerX showed an Intel-only 1.1.1 app with a different bundle ID, org.niltsh.MPlayerX.

limitation: I found no official source linking the scanned com.telephoto.identifier bundle or its reported build 107.114 to a current release.
notes: The upstream app’s architecture cannot be transferred to this listing without evidence linking the two bundle IDs.

name: iCUE
product: iCUE peripheral configuration software by Corsair

evidence.says: Corsair offers a Mac download whose iCUEInitialInstaller.app/Contents/MacOS/iCUEInitialInstaller binary is universal in bootstrap version 1.22.16.
Corsair's macOS setup guide says that iCUE uses Intel-based features and requires Rosetta on Apple silicon.
Corsair dates its latest general iCUE release, 5.54.46, to November 17, 2026 without specifying the Mac application's architecture.

limitation: The bootstrap archive contains no com.corsair.cue.main app, and the setup guide does not identify a release or say whether the installed main executable is Intel-only.
notes: The universal bootstrap uses a distinct bundle ID. Its architecture should not be applied to the installed application.

name: Blu-ray Player Pro
product: Mac Blu-ray Player Pro by Macgo International

evidence.says: Macgo’s update feed lists 3.3.23 as the newest release and identifies its exact download and March 15, 2025 release date.
Inspection of Blu-ray Player Pro.app/Contents/MacOS/Blu-ray Player and Info.plist found the exact bundle ID, version 3.3.23 build 250315, and an x86_64-only Mach-O.
The Japanese distributor lists Apple M1 and M2 support for the Pro edition.
The cask for 3.3.23 reports that the Intel app requires Rosetta 2 and is disabled in Homebrew.

limitation: The vendor’s update feed and DMG are live, but the old global product page is gone and ongoing maintenance could not be confirmed.
notes: Homebrew’s disabled status does not prevent direct download from the publisher’s update feed.

name: JPEGmini Lite
product: JPEGmini Lite by Beamr Imaging Ltd. (formerly ICVT)

evidence.says: The historical store catalog identifies JPEGmini Lite by Beamr Imaging Ltd., version 2.2.4, with Apple product ID 525742250.
Apple’s US Mac software lookup returns no current listing for the former JPEGmini Lite product ID.
The current vendor page offers JPEGmini and JPEGmini Pro releases but offers no separate Lite edition.

limitation: The final Lite build’s architecture and release date could not be verified.
notes: The vendor’s current Apple Silicon JPEGmini release is a different edition.

name: iStumbler
product: iStumbler by iStumbler Labs (Alf Watt)

evidence.says: The developer’s update feed announces iStumbler 2.0 as a new Mac app on November 25, 2026 with macOS 14 as the minimum but gives no CPU architecture.
Apple’s Mac software lookup identifies version 2.0 with the same net.istumbler bundle ID as the scanned release.
Inspection of iStumbler.app/Contents/MacOS/iStumbler and Info.plist in the older vendor DMG found version 103.43 with only an x86_64 Mach-O.

limitation: The new Mac App Store release’s arm64 or universal architecture has not been stated or inspected.
notes: The vendor’s legacy direct download is still Intel-only 103.43, while 2.0 is distributed through the Mac App Store.

name: Nutshell Apps
product: Original Nutshell Apps enterprise container by Nutshell Software Limited

evidence.says: The legacy Nutshell Apps Google Play listing uses the exact scanned identifier for its Android client.
Causeway says it acquired the Nutshell application in 2024 and provides a desktop container download for Mac.
The current Mac installer contains Nutshell Apps 2 version 3.0.3 with bundle ID com.nutshellapps.container.nutshell and an x86_64-only main executable.

limitation: I did not find a current official Mac build or documented architecture for the original com.nutshellapps.nutshellmobile listing.
notes: The original vendor has dissolved, and Causeway’s available Mac download is for the separately identified Nutshell Apps 2.
